subject: Choice of FI vs PI model

messages.author: 208520df5a1c57c2
messages.subject: Choice of FI vs PI model
parts:
Hi

I am analyzing data from an aerial cetacean survey using a Trial configuration. Normally in such analyses the PI assumption is preferred because responsive movement is not expected and PI models almost always have better fit and lower AIC than the equivalent FI models. However I have one case where FI does fit well and has lower AIC than the PI model. It also produces a substantially (+40%) higher estimate than the PI model, which is also something I didn't expect, given the issue of possible unmodelled hetergeneity with FI models.

My question is: Is there any reason not to prefer an FI model in a case like this? I don't see any assumption violations so I am inclined to accept the FI model.

Thanks,

Daniel Pike.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Choice of FI vs PI model
parts:
Daniel

Good question; I appreciate your inclination toward the point independence model for the reasons you provide.  Afraid I can't say anything about the difference in abundance estimates produced by the point and full independence models, and the estimates don't enter into the question of model selection.

Have a look through Section 5 of Buckland et al. (2010) where they analyse minke data from SCANS II, using tracker and primary configuration.  In their analysis, the full independence model produced the lowest AIC and they based their inference upon it.  This analysis is also discussed in Section 6.4.4.4 of Buckland et al. (2015).

Buckland, S. T., J. L. Laake, and D. L. Borchers. 2010. Double-observer line transect methods: levels of independence. Biometrics 66:169–177.
